Leveraging the AI for K-12 guidelines alongside cutting-edge personalized adaptive learning technologies, we propose an innovative AI education framework targeted at teachers and teacher educators. This framework will employ immersive virtual reality (VR) modules that simulate AI integration scenarios in classroom settings, complemented by collaborative AI-focused study networks employing peer-led inquiry and digital facilitation. This approach aims to significantly elevate AI awareness, expertise in AI content, and emotional receptivity towards AI, thereby advancing AI-related Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge (TPACK). We will assess the framework’s efficacy through a longitudinal mixed-methods study encompassing detailed pre- and post-intervention TPACK assessments, ethnographic classroom observations, and in-depth focus-group interviews to scrutinize persistent developments in AI integration and pedagogical transformation.

Professional development (PD) programs for teachers that utilize an adaptive AI-driven curriculum tailored to explicitly identified misconceptions and varying levels of AI-related experience will enhance teachers’ Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge (TPACK) more effectively than standard, non-adaptive PD programs. The adaptive curriculum will employ real-time analytics to assess teachers' misconceptions and knowledge gaps, leveraging machine learning algorithms to personalize the learning path with targeted content and pedagogical strategies. Improvements in TPACK will be measured using a validated TPACK assessment tool, ensuring the reliability and validity of results through pre- and post-program evaluations. The study will account for confounding factors by measuring prior exposure to AI technologies.

Leveraging collaborative learning communities among teachers, utilizing platforms such as Microsoft Teams and Edmodo, as an integral component of professional development (PD) programs will enhance teachers' AI-related Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge (TPACK) by facilitating peer-driven identification and correction of misconceptions. This method will utilize structured peer interactions focused on AI concepts and challenges, evaluated through a peer-assessment framework that incorporates criteria such as clarity, relevance, and resolution of misconceptions. The PD program will incorporate weekly moderated sessions, with facilitators guiding discussions and digital tools supporting collaborative activities. The program's effectiveness will be tested in diverse educational environments, comparing traditional individual-centric PD approaches with this collaborative model for measurable improvement in AI-related TPACK.

An integrative Professional Development (PD) model that combines AI-driven adaptive learning technologies with structured, collaborative teacher learning communities and ongoing feedback from expert facilitators will significantly enhance teachers' AI-related Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge (TPACK). The adaptive component will use machine learning algorithms to create personalized learning paths based on real-time analytics of teachers' performance and misconceptions. Collaborative communities will be facilitated via platforms such as Microsoft Teams, utilizing structured peer interactions to clarify AI concepts and address misconceptions. The PD model's effectiveness will be measured using a comprehensive TPACK assessment framework, ensuring reliability and validity. The study will include diverse educational contexts, control for prior AI exposure, and evaluate scalability across educational levels.

Teacher educators who participate in a structured training program based on the Intelligent-TPACK framework, which integrates specified ethical considerations, will exhibit significantly higher levels of AI-related Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge (TPACK) and exhibit decreased emotional resistance towards AI compared to those who undergo conventional TPACK training devoid of ethical components. This hypothesis will be assessed by implementing a two-week immersive workshop combining lectures, collaborative projects, and case studies on ethical AI integration, followed by pre- and post-training evaluations using validated TPACK and emotional response scales.

Implementing an interactive, AI-driven learning environment within teacher education programs, which leverages machine learning and natural language processing for personalized, real-time feedback, specifically through automated evaluations and adaptive content delivery, can significantly enhance teachers' Intelligent-TPACK. This approach integrates ethical knowledge by employing specific ethical scenarios and reflection activities into the learning modules, leading to improved AI-related Technological, Pedagogical, and Content Knowledge (TPACK) and ethical understanding. Furthermore, it positively influences teachers' emotional responses towards AI, comprising increased comfort and reduced anxiety, compared to traditional lecture-based methods, as measured by structured psychometric assessments.
